assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme behind biological nitrogen fixation, and the crystal structures of the FeMo cofactor, including the central light atom, make it a landmark of structure-driven mechanistic chemistry. Importance, originality and lasting impact are very high, and it ties to industrial ammonia chemistry and ongoing synthetic cluster and catalyst design.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the first crystal structures and cofactor architecture, and Einsle supplied the high-resolution structure that located the central carbon. Seefeldt and Dean, and Ribbe, made decisive biochemical and spectroscopic contributions. A three-person prize can be supported, but Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt overlap and fairly allocating credit among them is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The cofactor structure is independently confirmed by many groups and decades of crystallography, spectroscopy and biochemistry. Timing is reasonable, though substrate-binding and turnover intermediates are still being worked out, so recognition could be seen as slightly early on the mechanism.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site are not fully settled, so the prize motivation would have to focus on structure.
Credit among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe is contested, and I cannot verify exact priority from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing allows programmable single-nucleotide chemical conversion of DNA without double-strand breaks. It is a clear case of molecular design creating an enabling method used by a whole community, and it is already in clinical use. Importance and clarity of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the evident originator of both cytosine and adenine base editors. Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees on the key papers, and a prize would normally centre on Liu. The longlist also lists Liu under prime editing and DNA-encoded libraries, so a compound claim needs a clean, single-discovery motivation.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is extensive and clinical translation is advancing, so the technique is mature enough. The recent CRISPR prize (2020) may weigh on whether the committee sees this as a distinct chemistry advance, and long-term safety data are still accumulating.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing affects how the discovery is framed.
Whether the committee would credit Komor or Gaudelli alongside Liu is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architecture and active sites underpins petrochemical refining and emissions control at huge scale. Structure directly explains function, and there is a long record of designed frameworks with real applications. Importance is high.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and industrial implementation), Davis (synthesis and structure-directing agents) and Zones (organic structure-directing agents, Chevron zeolites such as SSZ-13, used in NOx control) are credible leaders. Many other contributors (Tsapatsis, Jihong Yu and others) have a claim, and the field is broad rather than a single discovery. I have professional proximity to this field and treat my own judgement cautiously.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature and its impact is confirmed over decades of use. The question is more whether a single sharp discovery can be named, since the zeolite field has previously been recognised only indirectly.
uncertainties: It is not a single discovery, which makes a short prize motivation hard.
Priority between academic and industrial inventors is hard to assess from the supplied credit list.
My own field proximity could bias me toward it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts have reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by maximizing atom efficiency and bridging homogeneous and heterogeneous concepts, and they have been enabled by aberration-corrected electron microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy. Impact on the field is large and growing.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Nature Chemistry paper by Zhang, Qiao, Wang, Liu, Li and collaborators coined the concept and is the usual starting point. Datye and Liu contributed strong STEM evidence, and others had earlier related work on isolated atoms. The credit set is crowded and allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely reproduced, but the structural proof depends on local-probe techniques, and the true nature of active sites under reaction conditions is often debated. Industrial relevance is still emerging, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Active-site nature under operando conditions is frequently contested and structural claims need careful scrutiny.
Priority relative to earlier isolated-atom catalysis work is uncertain.
Practical application is not yet proven at scale.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers lets structures be solved from nanocrystals and enables time-resolved molecular movies, overcoming radiation-damage limits. This is an enabling structural method with strong appeal to a structural chemist, and the impact is high.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle experiments with Fromme, Hajdu and colleagues, and Schlichting contributed to time-resolved applications and instrumentation. Hajdu may no longer be eligible, and I cannot verify his status; I propose only living names I believe eligible. Many facility and instrument contributors complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: The method is established and increasingly routine at multiple XFELs, and independent groups have validated it. Its reach into chemistry rather than biology and its competition with cryo-EM and microED may influence how timely the committee considers it.
uncertainties: Eligibility of some credited individuals cannot be verified from the supplied text.
Impact beyond a limited number of XFEL beamlines is still developing.
Competition with microED and cryo-EM may reduce perceived necessity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides obtained by selective etching of MAX phases. The designed layered architecture and tunable surface chemistry give new functions in energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. Originality is clear, and structural characterization is solid.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum reported Ti3C2 in 2011 (with colleagues at Drexel), and the three-name configuration is natural. Barsoum's MAX-phase foundation is the key precursor, and Gogotsi drove most of the subsequent growth of the field.
assessment.maturity: Thousands of independent studies confirm the family, but applications are still maturing and commercial uses are limited. Recognition could be timely or slightly early.
uncertainties: Real-world applications are not yet clearly established.
Surface termination control and reproducibility across labs remain imperfectly understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, from PROTACs to molecular glues, introduces a new modality in which small molecules induce proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system. It is a conceptual and structural advance, with the cereblon and thalidomide mechanism, and is already in the clinic.
assessment.attribution: Crews conceived PROTACs and developed the concept; Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL ligand and ternary-complex design; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Deshaies, Sakamoto and others have credit claims, and the prize configuration is difficult with eight credited names. The discovery is a compound of PROTACs and molecular glues.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are advancing and the mechanisms are well supported, but approved degraders are not yet established. Recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose parts may require different recognition.
No approved PROTAC drug yet, so clinical validation is incomplete.
Credit among many contributors is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas extended pore control from micropores to 2-50 nm and opened a family of designed porous solids with tunable structure. The concept is original and widely used in catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting, and the structural characterization (electron microscopy and diffraction) is convincing.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil team (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) reported MCM-41, with Ryoo's work on ordered carbons and Stucky's SBA-15 and Zhao as key subsequent contributions. Allocation among industrial and academic groups is uncertain, and Inagaki's independent route adds a further claim.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature and the discovery is firmly confirmed. Real commercial impact is more limited than for zeolites, and the 2025 MOF prize may reduce the appetite for another porous-materials recognition so soon.
uncertainties: Industrial impact is modest relative to zeolites.
Recent porous-materials recognition could reduce its priority.
Credit between Mobil researchers, Kuroda, Inagaki and later academic groups is complicated.
